newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish higher, but off peaks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish higher, but off peaks.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed higher, but profit-taking nudged most contracts off session peaks, traders said.
They also said comments from U.S. Federal Reserve officials contributed to the slight pullback, which for several minutes pushed June T-bonds below support at 107-26/32.

On Wednesday afternoon, U.S. Federal Reserve governor Laurence Meyer said the U.S. economy was growing strongly at a rate well above its long-term trend. He said first-quarter growth looks to have been close to a four percent annualized pace, nearly twice the economy's perceived trend growth rate.
Meyer's comments to the Fed's Consumer Advisory Council came on the heels of Kansas City Federal Reserve president Thomas Hoenig's statements at a joint board meeting of the Kansas City Fed.

Hoenig said the U.S. economy continues to grow at a solid pace with tight labor markets, strong consumer demand and moderate inflation. He said signs of inflation pressure appear in the U.S. unemployment rate and the capacity utilization rate within the manufacturing sector.
The comments failed to spark major selling, as the bearish tone in the market has already been eradicated due to U.S. economic reports showing a stable to slightly lower growth rate.
The April Philadelphia Federal Reserve business index fell to 5.7, compared to average trade estimates for a slim decline to 20.4 from March's 21.1.

U.S. weekly jobless claims, which were released earlier on Thursday, rose to 332,000, versus average trade estimates for 317,000. Claims in the prior week were upwardly revised to 324,000, from 318,000.
June T-bonds and September Eurodollars rose to the highest levels in two-and-a-half weeks in reaction to the reports.

Although both contracts retreated from the highs, June T-bonds managed to close above the 20-day moving average of 107-22/32. This is the first time the contract has closed above the 20-day moving average since February 26, an analyst said.
Several floor traders and analysts said the tone was constructive ahead of Friday, and that the market may close higher for the week for the first time in about eight weeks in a row.

At the end of pit trade, June T-bonds were 12/32 higher at 107-27/32, June 10-year notes were up 08/32 at 105-30/32, September Eurodollars were up 0.04 at 93.745, and September T-bills were up 0.03 at 94.325. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
